correctness.rationale: All 1023 nonzero forms are tested with projective-chart Gröbner unit ideals, giving 336 geometrically smooth; rational incidence leaves 154 tangent-filling. Exhaustive XOR constructions give 392 pencils and exactly eight three-spaces. A distinct 512 linear-evaluation splitting search reproduces the eight mask sets. Explicit 168-element PGL action has an eight-net orbit, stabilizer order 21, and transitive seven-member stabilizer action. Every member has three rational flexes on a rational line; the seven supports in each net exhaust all seven Fano lines. Any four-space contains fifteen 3-spaces, contradicting the global count eight. Exact code and outputs accompany the claim.

originality.rationale: The classified objects are seven-member all-smooth AND tangent-filling binary cubic nets, with a sharp maximum dimension and a Fano-line/Singer correspondence. Asgarli–Ghioca (2023) defines tangent-filling and proves degree bounds but not net compatibility; Asgarli–Ghioca–Reichstein (2022) treats all-smooth systems without dual-line covering; Ishitsuka (2016) gives individual cubic classes, including flex data, but not seven-member net enumeration. Three targeted published-finding corpus queries and literature searches found no direct or implied same-statement result. Exhaustive mathematical comparison remains qualified by possible unindexed finite-geometry work.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier finite-geometric or computational catalogues could contain an equivalent compatible-net census.
The individual three-flex binary cubic class is published; priority attaches only to the complete simultaneous net classification and its maximality/geometry.

value.rationale: The theorem simultaneously classifies smoothness and the tangent-covering property across every rational member of a linear system, with a sharp maximal dimension, unique eight-element orbit, rational-Fano-line support and stabilizer/Singer subgroup correspondence.
